Ghost of Tsushima is a stunning and immersive adventure. Its beautiful open world, fluid combat, and emotionally grounded story make every moment memorable. A breathtaking blend of art, action, and atmosphere.
I was looking for a game to really get into, and let me say this consumed my focus and i need to play it every waking moment now.

I completed the game on Playstation and then bought it again on steam to play it again. combat is challenging but not too frustrating, secondary gameplay aspects like shrines fit more diegetically than other open world games tend to.

I'm enjoying this game immensely. It reminds me of AC: Odyssey, but is different in several ways. I like that I can just wander the land and pet foxes, or get into some fun battles. I like that I can run in and fight or take the stealthy approach. The story is rich, the characters interesting, the landscape beautiful. Get this game. You won't regret it.

THIS GAME CARES ABOUT YOUR HARDWARE. Let me talk about the optimization. Its done so well that it makes me wonder why other AAA titles that look worse, are so bad. Most modern games I play now a days gets my CPU and GPU temps so high in 4K. How does a game look so magically beautiful graphically and visually, and still manage to not exceed the average temps?

That aside, this is a must buy. The combat is fluid, and at no point do you get tired of it. The branching techniques keep things fresh. The story is above average, and justifies the gameplay. There is nothing more I can say. A visual masterpiece, and solid fun until the end. Solid 9/10 from me.
The level of polish is excellent, the performance is butter smooth, the graphics are beautiful and combat is satisfying. What else could we ever need?

A nice reprieve from getting stuffed in Elden Ring with a more linear story yet open world. Combat feels great.

A game of quality paradoxes. Combat is amazing and extremely well fleshed-out but because of extremely repetetive encounters it becomes a chore about halfway through. The world is incredibly beautiful and feels like a ukiyo-e painting you walked into but gets spoiled by repetetive activities you find in it and weak side quests. The fact that you step into mongol/bandit patrols at almost every turn is also really bad and makes exploring less fun. The story is pretty good but gets undercut by the main character who lacks depth which is kinda fixed in the DLC but it's too late too little. Also the game has weird design choices which make the experience worse: no ability to pass time which is criminal in an open world game, weather changes into thunderstorms all the time during late game so you have to use the freaking flute non stop which is another thing that spoils exploration and you can only load save game files from the main menu which is BS. I'm glad i played this game but propably never will again. I hope the sequel is better.

So I finished the main story, but not the DLC content yet.

I really enjoyed the game, because it reminded me of some stuff that I liked about buddhism.

It allows people to take gorgeous screenshots throughout the game, because some areas are really very beautiful.

Some bosses can be very challenging, but the game holds your hand in the form of wind, which points you to the direction where you should go for the tracked quest.

Overall, I recommend the game, because it is a quality product altogether. The game didn't crash during my playthrough, the gameplay was fluent. So, this is it for my short review. Looking forward to playing Ghost of Yotei, when it comes out on PC.

This is without a doubt the best game i've ever played. The plot and the story mixed with the samurai theme. And defying what you've known for freedom, Is absolutely a masterpiece. I wish i could wipe my memory of the walkthroughs and play it again so the plot twists were brand new to me.

I absolutely love this game. The combat is great and very engaging. Sneaking around trying to take down a camp without getting spotted is always a fun challenge. The world is beautiful and it's a lot of fun getting distracted while you are on your way to the next objective. I often forget said objective and end up doing a bunch of unplanned stuff. Highly recommend!

This is truly an amazing and unforgettable game. Since it was my first time playing I mostly just stuck to the story missions and a handful of side ones, and still took about 25 hours to finish the game. Graphically this game is beautiful I was running on high settings with a 2070 Super and didn’t drop below 70fps the entire game, every time you’re in a field or climbing a mountain the game feels like one beautiful cinematic. Combat is great and really lets you play your way, some missions railroad you into stealth for a few minutes but otherwise there’s no required stealth and open world combat is whatever you want it to be. The story was great, all the characters felt unique for the most part, and the dialogue was incredible especially between lord Shimura and Jin. Truly a 10/10
Great game, amazing and emotional story, exceptional combat. Good value too, I got plenty of hours out of it for the price.
Very good port that works good on PC and steam deck. Was happy there were immediate updates to fix any problems. Game itself is a beautiful open world game with good sword combat and fun stealth.

Beautiful game. Highly recommend getting lost in the world of Tsushima. 

I go back and forth between my PC and steam deck and am extremely happy with the performance on both.

I really tried to like this game, but outside of the visuals it just falls flat. The game looks gorgeous, but it is SO BORING especially by the time you get to act 3. I might come back just to finish the game one day, but there's nothing but a bland story, bland fighting, and bland open world, so if I come back to it it'll be a very long time from now.

Pros: Absolutely beautiful game

Cons: Boring combat, action button will pick up items when your mid fight trying to change your stance, sub menus for using sticky bombs, smoke bombs, different arrows, etc are several button presses and extremely inconvenient to use during combat, story is bland and the game feels like a worse assassin's creed with less features. Frequent crashes, both on trying to boot the game up and when I'm playing it crashes me out of the game, probably a couple times every time I try to play. Textures in places are broken and flickering lights and items. I expect more polish from a triple A title like this.

I got this on sale but it definitely wasn't worth 44$

Overall the game is nice to look at, but that's the only thing it has going for it.

I've been beta testing Sony's first-party games on my PS5 Pro for years. Unfortunately, Sony's decision to phase out the physical disc drive shows that greed has no limits. This will be my last PlayStation generation. I won't support a digital-only future.
I know it sounds ironic because I also buy digital games on PC. But on PC, I have a choice. I can buy games from different stores that compete on price. On PlayStation, Sony controls the entire digital storefront, and that's exactly why physical discs still matter.
